issue.title: Mockito confuses varargs and single-param methods (regression)
issue.body:
In Mockito 2.2.5 and later, when setting expectations for mocking a varargs method, using an array doesn't work:
```Java
Mockito.when(good.call(Mockito.any(String[].class))).thenReturn(1L);
```
And instead the contained type must be used:
```Java
Mockito.when(good.call(Mockito.any(String.class))).thenReturn(1L);
```
However in the face of an overload of the varargs method that takes a single argument (of the same type):
```Java
    Long call(String value);
    Long call(String... values);
```
This results in being unable to set an expectation for the varargs call.
This worked previously in Mockito 2.2.4 and earlier.

Reproducer: [mockito-bug.tar.gz](https://github.com/mockito/mockito/files/2769668/mockito-bug.tar.gz)

input.args: Issue 1593: Mockito confuses varargs and single-param methods (regression). Reporter says any(String[].class) does not match varargs call in 2.2.5+, and with overloads call(String) and call(String...), a stub for the varargs call cannot be set. Evidence opened: mockito-core/src/main/java/org/mockito/ArgumentMatchers.java (any(Class) javadoc: since 5.0.0 matches varargs when array type given).

final: {"number": 1593, "label": "bug", "route": "repro-check", "related": [2796, 3786], "evidence": ["mockito/mockito-core/src/main/java/org/mockito/ArgumentMatchers.java"], "reply": "Thanks for the report. The version range (2.2.4 vs 2.2.5 and later), the code snippet, and the expected and actual behaviour are all clear, so this can be reproduced as written. The matcher in question is ArgumentMatchers.any(Class), which is where I would start looking. Note that its current Javadoc says that since Mockito 5.0.0 it can match varargs when the array type is given, such as any(String[].class). Could you check whether the overload case (call(String) next to call(String...)) still fails on the latest release?"}
